newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares soar on hopes of end to crisis.
newsitem.headline: India shares soar on hopes of end to crisis.

text.p: Indian stocks raced ahead on Wednesday amid mounting optimism that talks between the government and its key Congress ally will end an 11-day-old political crisis, analysts said.
The key result of ending the dispute would be that a pro-market fiscal budget for 1997/98 would be left intact, analysts said.
By 1500 local time (0930 GMT), Bombay's benchmark stock index had surged 111.6 points, or 3.2 percent, to 3,632.09.
"Broadly, we are back to the same levels of when the crisis started," Sandeep Dhingra, equity analyst at SSKI Securities, told Reuters.

Congress has withdrawn its make-or-break support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 10-month-old minority government, citing economic failure among other reasons. A parliamentary vote of confidence is scheduled for Friday.
The ruling United Front alliance and Congress were due to begin talks on Wednesday to try to resolve the dispute.
"We expect the talks to start in the course of the day," United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy said.
Analysts said the proposed meeting has raised hopes of both sides resolving their differences. "One can selectively start buying (stocks)," Dhingra said.
"The market is really sensitive to political developments taking place in New Delhi," said Piyush Vora, a member-broker of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
The Bombay index crashed more than eight percent after the Congress announcement, but has since recovered on hopes the political drama will leave the budget unscathed.
"The budget looks to be intact. That's the main issue for the market," said Ramdeo Agarwal, research head at Motilal Oswal Securities.
The budget proposals unveiled on February 28 slash corporate and personal taxes, lower import tariffs and legalise company share buy-backs.
The widely acclaimed budget had been expected to be passed on April 21. There is now no indication as to when a budget vote can be taken.
"Everybody is waiting for the vote. We expect the market to go up substantially if the budget is passed," said Tushar Sarda, president and chief executive at Daewoo Securities.
Lingering doubts ahead of the confidence vote would restrict strong buying, with the market reading into every bit of news coming from New Delhi, analysts said.
"Foreign funds have to buy at some level of certainty," Motilal Oswal's Agarwal said.
